'''Yves Laszlo''' ({{IPA|fr|iv laslo}} born 4 April 1964) is a [[French people|French]] [[mathematician]] working in the [[University of Paris-Sud]].  He specializes in [[algebraic geometry]].

Laszlo obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1988 from the University of Paris-Sud under the supervision of [[Arnaud Beauville]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=59622 }}</ref>
He started the Fondation Mathématique Jacques Hadamard in 2011, and directed it until 2012.<ref>[http://www.campus-paris-saclay.fr/content/download/2183/13788/version/1/file/121120+CP+Hans+Rugh.pdf Hans Rugh remplace Yves Laszlo à la Fondation mathématique Jacques Hadamard] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150411205330/http://www.campus-paris-saclay.fr/content/download/2183/13788/version/1/file/121120+CP+Hans+Rugh.pdf |date=April 11, 2015 }}, Press release, November 20, 2012.</ref>

The [[Beauville–Laszlo theorem]] on gluing [[sheaf (mathematics)|sheaves]] together is named after Laszlo and Beauville, who published it in 1995.<ref>{{Citation
 | last=Beauville
 | first=Arnaud
 | author-link=Arnaud Beauville
 | last2=Laszlo
 | first2=Yves
 | author2-link=Yves Laszlo

 | journal=Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I
 | volume=320
 | issue=3
 | pages=335–340
 | issn=0764-4442
 | url=http://math1.unice.fr/~beauvill/pubs/descente.pdf
 | access-date=2008-04-08
}}.</ref>
